standard_prerequisites.name: The properties of the diagonal of a morphism of algebraic spaces
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, label spaces-morphisms-lemma-properties-diagonal (invoked at proof line 3655)
standard_prerequisites.use: It gives that $\Delta$ is representable, separated, a monomorphism and locally of finite type, which is the starting point; representability makes the fibre product $V$ below a scheme.

standard_prerequisites.name: Closed immersions are detected etale locally on the target
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, label spaces-morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion-local (invoked at proof line 3660)
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the closedness of $\Delta$ to the closedness of the map $V \to U$ obtained from an affine etale $U \to X \times_Y X$.

standard_prerequisites.name: The resulting auxiliary scheme is Noetherian, of finite type and quasi-compact
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, labels spaces-morphisms-lemma-composition-finite-type, spaces-morphisms-lemma-base-change-finite-type and spaces-morphisms-lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-noetherian (invoked at proof lines 3662-3665)
standard_prerequisites.use: They make $U$ Noetherian and, together with quasi-separatedness of $f$, show that $V \to U$ is a quasi-compact morphism of finite type, so that the valuative criterion applies.

standard_prerequisites.name: The valuative criterion of properness for a morphism of Noetherian schemes
standard_prerequisites.use: Once the uniqueness of the dotted arrow is verified for all discrete valuation ring diagrams over $U$, it gives that $V \to U$ is proper.

standard_prerequisites.name: A proper monomorphism is a closed immersion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Etale Morphisms, label etale-lemma-characterize-closed-immersion (invoked at proof line 3684)
standard_prerequisites.use: Since $\Delta$ is a monomorphism and has been shown proper, it is a closed immersion, i.e. $f$ is separated.

core_obligations: Reduce the claim to showing that the diagonal $\Delta : X \to X \times_Y X$ is a closed immersion, and use the known properties of the diagonal to choose an affine etale $U \to X \times_Y X$ with $V = X \times_{\Delta} U$ (proof lines 3652-3657).

Reduce further to the closedness of $V \to U$, and record that $U$ is Noetherian, $V$ is a scheme because $\Delta$ is representable, $V$ is quasi-compact because $f$ is quasi-separated, and hence $V \to U$ is of finite type (proof lines 3658-3668).

Verify the valuative criterion: a discretely valued diagram over $U$ encodes a pair $a, b : \Spec(A) \to X$ agreeing over $Y$ and equal over $K$, so assumption (3) forces $a = b$ and produces the dotted arrow (proof lines 3669-3680).

Conclude with the properness criterion over Noetherian schemes that $V \to U$ is proper, so $\Delta$ is proper, and since $\Delta$ is a monomorphism it is a closed immersion, which means $f$ is separated (proof lines 3681-3685).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the diagonal and the auxiliary diagrams (proof lines 3652-3657).
The auxiliary schemes and their finiteness properties (proof lines 3658-3668).
Properness, then closedness of the diagonal (proof lines 3681-3685).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a valuative criterion for separatedness of a morphism of algebraic spaces: if every diagram from the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring into the source filling a diagram over the target has at most one lift, then the morphism is separated (statement lines 3631-3649). The proof translates the claim into closedness of the diagonal, descends to an affine etale cover of the square where the base change of the diagonal becomes a quasi-compact finite type morphism of Noetherian schemes, verifies the valuative criterion there by reading a diagram as a pair of morphisms agreeing over the base and over the fraction field, and concludes properness and hence closedness. The valuative verification and the local reduction are the substance, so the claim is H2.
